samples.summary: Task doc still describes the old contract of the shipped code: "strip config carriers to a **fixpoint** rather than one pass" (line 41) and the checked item "`stripConfigDirectives()` loops until the source stops changing" (line 47). The implementation is deliberately NOT a fixpoint — it is bounded at `MAX_STRIP_PASSES` and REFUSES the fence (returns `null`) when the source is still changing, and it now also gained a `MAX_FENCE_CHARS` length cap plus three source-refusal checks (`FETCH_TAG_RE`, `IMAGE_METADATA_RE`, `CSS_SOURCE_FETCH_RE`) that the checklist and "Deliberately not done" section never mention. Anyone reading this active task doc to understand the shipped guard gets the wrong contract (an unbounded loop that never refuses).

samples.summary: `withRealEngine()` mutates two process-global singletons shared with every other case in the notes suite and does not fully restore them: `SVGElement.prototype.getBBox`/`getComputedTextLength` do not exist in jsdom, so the `finally` block assigns `undefined` back, leaving own properties on the prototype whose presence-based feature detection (`if (el.getBBox)` is falsy but `'getBBox' in el` is now true) differs from the pristine environment for later cases in the same worker (CodeMirror/KaTeX cases in this same file). It also leaves the real `mermaid` module loaded and, via `mermaidAPI.globalReset()`, its site config wiped — benign today only because `resetMermaidStateForTests()` clears `initializedTheme` in `beforeEach`, i.e. the isolation depends on an invariant in mermaid.ts rather than on this helper.
samples.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/preview.test.ts:707-712 saves possibly-undefined prototype methods and restores them unconditionally; packages/notes/src/view/mermaid.ts:717-723 is what actually keeps the leaked engine state from affecting later cases.
